//@version=5
indicator("uct-rsi-atr-parity-v1", overlay=false)
rsi14 = ta.rsi(close, 14)
atr14 = ta.atr(14)
plot(rsi14, title="rsi14")
plot(atr14, title="atr14")

provenance.note: Captured via CSV export (Table view -> Download data) of a real SPY Daily chart with a live ta.rsi(close,14)/ta.atr(14) indicator added, full double-precision floats (not Table-view-display rounding). 1,328 real trading-day bars (2021-05-24 .. 2026-09-04), ALL rows carry a real vendor value (not a single probe row) -- deliberately avoiding Lane B's first-pass single-probe overclaim (RISK-018b amendment). The chart's history buffer was scrolled/loaded further back before export specifically to get a long enough runway to separate a genuine period-warmup (14 bars) from the much longer (~170-bar) seed-convergence lag caused by feeding UCT a finite captured window rather than the vendor's continuous multi-decade history -- see _vendor_parity_warmup_bars' note.

_vendor_parity_warmup_bars_note: 180 is NOT the semantic period-warmup (that is 14 bars -- the first index at which UCT's rsi(close,14) is computable at all). It is a conservative round number past the empirically observed convergence point (last disagreeing index measured at 172 of 1328) for a SEPARATE effect: UCT's Wilder/RMA recursion re-seeds cold at THIS capture window's own first bar, while the real vendor value at every one of these calendar dates already reflects TradingView's continuous smoothing since SPY's real 1993 inception (already fully converged). Comparing bars 14-179 against a fully-converged vendor value would read as a formula disagreement (up to ~25% relative at bar 14) when it is a capture-methodology artifact -- exactly the misclassification risk the Tranche 2 readiness report named. Bars 180+ (1,148 of 1,328) are genuine steady-state comparisons, converging to ~1e-9 relative delta (pure float noise).
